- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is flat or trending down, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in bearish reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70) and forecast is still rising, cap forecast at 70–72.  
- For 30-day horizon, if last 3–5 days of true values show strong downward trend, model often underestimates drop; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.48, -0.72), forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–2% per negative sentiment event.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome by 5–10% over 3–5 days, model is underestimating volatility; increase forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
